Silhouettes are small and positive (CT 0.013, RNA 0.079, WSI 0.050, WXS 0.091), and within-label distances exceed between-label distances by only a small margin in each modality. Negative fractions are high (CT 0.44, WSI 0.46, RNA 0.28, WXS 0.26), meaning a substantial minority of patients are closer to the competing set than to their own. The overall native-view pattern is therefore weak and partially conflicting: RNA and WXS give the clearest (though still small) positive separation, while CT and WSI show near-zero separation with the highest overlap. No modality shows strong boundary representation, and no nearest competing set is reported.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002, native patient-geometry membership representation is coherently positive but modest across all four modalities. Silhouettes are positive in CT (0.069), RNA (0.096), WSI (0.204), and WXS (0.275), with within-set distances below between-set distances in every modality. Negative fractions are low (CT 0.10, RNA 0.27, WSI 0.08, WXS 0.02), indicating limited geometric overlap with the competing set. The nearest competing set is K2_C0001 in all four modalities. The overall native-view pattern for this set is coherent and weakly-to-moderately supportive of current membership, with WXS and WSI providing the clearest separation; this is membership-representation evidence only and does not by itself determine accept or drop.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: This set-scope result is consistent with the prior pair-scope affinity_geometry_concordance report, which found small positive pair-boundary silhouettes (CT 0.013, RNA 0.079, WSI 0.050, WXS 0.091) and high negative fractions in CT and WSI. The set-scope decomposition shows that the pair-level positive separation is carried mainly by K2_C0002, while K2_C0001 is near-zero or negative in CT, WSI, and WXS. Prior structural_diagnostics reports for K2_C0002 found a single-cluster-dominated internal screen (candidate_k=1) with only weak, modality-inconsistent native-view separation for feasible k>=2 splits, which is separate internal-subdivision evidence and does not bear on membership representation. Prior RNA pathway enrichment describes a coherent transcriptomic phenotype for K2_C0002, but that is biological-identity evidence and does not establish geometric membership representation.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: K2_C0002 shows a coherent transcriptomic phenotype that is largely the mirror image of K2_C0001: coordinated down-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation, interferon (alpha and gamma) responses, immune/allograft activation, DNA repair, ROS, mTORC1, and cell-cycle (E2F, G2M) programs, with up-regulation of TGF-beta, Hedgehog, Wnt/beta-catenin, and UV-response-down programs. Leading-edge gene sets are internally consistent and overlap heavily with those in K2_C0001 (same OXPHOS and interferon gene members), indicating the two sets differ along shared molecular axes rather than unrelated programs. Magnitudes are moderate-to-strong (|NES| ~1.4-2.3) with FDR q values from 0.001 to ~0.04.
biological_support.cross_evidence_context: This is the reciprocal set-versus-rest contrast to K2_C0001; the two reports describe the same comparison from opposite sides and therefore are not independent biological confirmations. The structural diagnostics for K2_C0002 (dominant single-cluster resolution, candidate_k=1) and the pair-level affinity geometry are separate evidence streams and do not alter the transcriptomic phenotype interpretation.
limitations: Enrichment is relative to the rest of the current partition, not an external reference population.
With exactly two sets, the two set-versus-rest contrasts are reciprocal, not independent confirmations.
FDR q values near 0.04-0.05 (e.g., EMT, inflammatory response, cholesterol homeostasis) are weaker and should be weighted accordingly.
Pathway enrichment reflects a ranked Wald-statistic contrast and does not establish causal or clinical meaning.
Biological identity alone does not establish that current membership or granularity deserves retention.

Leading-edge gene sets are internally consistent and overlap heavily with those in K2_C0001 (same OXPHOS and interferon gene members), indicating the two sets differ along shared molecular axes rather than unrelated programs. Magnitudes are moderate-to-strong (|NES| ~1.4-2.3) with FDR q values from 0.001 to ~0.04.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This is the reciprocal set-versus-rest contrast to K2_C0001; the two reports describe the same comparison from opposite sides and therefore are not independent biological confirmations. The structural diagnostics for K2_C0002 (dominant single-cluster resolution, candidate_k=1) and the pair-level affinity geometry are separate evidence streams and do not alter the transcriptomic phenotype interpretation.
limitations: Enrichment is relative to the rest of the current partition, not an external reference population.
With exactly two sets, the two set-versus-rest contrasts are reciprocal, not independent confirmations.
FDR q values near 0.04-0.05 (e.g., EMT, inflammatory response, cholesterol homeostasis) are weaker and should be weighted accordingly.
Pathway enrichment reflects a ranked Wald-statistic contrast and does not establish causal or clinical meaning.
Biological identity alone does not establish that current membership or granularity deserves retention.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Across all four native patient geometries the current pair boundary is only weakly represented. Silhouettes are small and positive (CT 0.013, RNA 0.079, WSI 0.050, WXS 0.091), and within-label distances exceed between-label distances by only a small margin in each modality. Negative fractions are high (CT 0.44, WSI 0.46, RNA 0.28, WXS 0.26), meaning a substantial minority of patients are closer to the competing set than to their own. The overall native-view pattern is therefore weak and partially conflicting: RNA and WXS give the clearest (though still small) positive separation, while CT and WSI show near-zero separation with the highest overlap. No modality shows strong boundary representation, and no nearest competing set is reported.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This pair-scope boundary evidence is distinct from the set-scope structural diagnostics, which found a dominant single-cluster resolution (candidate_k=1) for both sets and thus no internal subdivision signal. The weak pair-boundary representation here concerns the boundary between K2_C0001 and K2_C0002, not internal structure, and does not by itself determine whether the pair should be merged.
limitations: Silhouette values are small and near zero; they indicate limited geometric support for the current boundary rather than a definitive separation or its absence.
High negative fractions in CT and WSI indicate material cross-modal disagreement in boundary representation.
No nearest competing set is reported, so the closest alternative label is not identified.
Native-view alignment is not external validation and does not establish biological or clinical meaning.
This evidence does not itself determine whether the pair should be merged.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002 the dominant spectral gap is at the single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.8582 at k=1, dropping to 0.080 at k=2 and lower thereafter), so this screening calculation does not show a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal. Feasible k>=2 solutions are reported: the k=2 split has moderate consensus separation (silhouette 0.435, negative fraction 0.0, unbalanced children 11/37) and a relatively low normalized cut (0.887), with native-view separation weak in CT (-0.005), RNA (0.086), and WSI (0.118) but moderate in WXS (0.248). Higher-k solutions show weaker consensus separation and near-zero or negative native-view separation. The overall pattern is a single dominant cluster with only weak, modality-inconsistent support for any finer subdivision.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This set-scope internal-subdivision evidence is separate from the pair-scope boundary representation and from the transcriptomic phenotype. The absence of a dominant subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about whether K2_C0002 is independent from neighboring candidates. The weak native-view separation of the feasible k=2 split is consistent with the weak pair-boundary representation seen in the affinity geometry.
limitations: Structural diagnostics are triage evidence and do not independently establish retention, split, or merge.
The geometry basis is candidate-generation consensus, not external validation or a stability score.

reports.dimension_interpretation: The current pair boundary is moderately represented in candidate-consensus geometry: agreement with an independent two-way spectral partition is moderately high (ARI 0.744), and within-side affinity (0.645) exceeds between-side affinity (0.397). The normalized-cut cost of the current boundary is moderate (0.773), reflecting non-trivial cross-boundary connectivity rather than strong graph separation. The union spectral structure is dominated by the single-cluster resolution (candidate_k=1, leading eigengap 0.698 versus 0.144 at k=2), which is merge-compatible evidence and must not be read as evidence for preserving the two-set boundary. Taken together, a represented current boundary combined with a single-cluster-dominated union is conflicting structural evidence, not automatic evidence against merge. This is pair-scope boundary and union-structure evidence only; it does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity and does not determine accept, drop, split, or merge.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior pair-scope affinity-geometry concordance across CT, WSI, RNA, and WXS showed only weak and partially conflicting native-view boundary representation (small positive silhouettes, high negative fractions in CT and WSI), while the prior partition-scope structural screen reported candidate_k=1 for both sets and lower nearest-pair between-set affinity (0.397) than within-set affinity. The present pair-scope structural diagnostics agree on moderate boundary representation in candidate-consensus geometry and a single-cluster-dominated union, but the native-view evidence remains weak and modality-inconsistent.
limitations: Structural diagnostics are triage evidence and do not independently establish retention, split, or merge.
The geometry basis is candidate-generation consensus, not external validation or a stability score.
The normalized-cut cost has opposite direction to separation measures; a moderate value reflects cross-boundary connectivity and is not a threshold or standalone merge rule.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002, native patient-geometry membership representation is coherently positive but modest across all four modalities. Silhouettes are positive in CT (0.069), RNA (0.096), WSI (0.204), and WXS (0.275), with within-set distances below between-set distances in every modality. Negative fractions are low (CT 0.10, RNA 0.27, WSI 0.08, WXS 0.02), indicating limited geometric overlap with the competing set. The nearest competing set is K2_C0001 in all four modalities. The overall native-view pattern for this set is coherent and weakly-to-moderately supportive of current membership, with WXS and WSI providing the clearest separation; this is membership-representation evidence only and does not by itself determine accept or drop.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This set-scope result is consistent with the prior pair-scope affinity_geometry_concordance report, which found small positive pair-boundary silhouettes (CT 0.013, RNA 0.079, WSI 0.050, WXS 0.091) and high negative fractions in CT and WSI. The set-scope decomposition shows that the pair-level positive separation is carried mainly by K2_C0002, while K2_C0001 is near-zero or negative in CT, WSI, and WXS. Prior structural_diagnostics reports for K2_C0002 found a single-cluster-dominated internal screen (candidate_k=1) with only weak, modality-inconsistent native-view separation for feasible k>=2 splits, which is separate internal-subdivision evidence and does not bear on membership representation. Prior RNA pathway enrichment describes a coherent transcriptomic phenotype for K2_C0002, but that is biological-identity evidence and does not establish geometric membership representation.
limitations: Silhouette values are small to moderate; they indicate limited-to-modest geometric support for current membership rather than a definitive separation.
Native-view alignment is not external validation and does not establish biological or clinical meaning.
The four native views are not votes; the pattern is reported jointly rather than resolved by majority or unanimity.
RNA negative fraction (0.27) indicates a non-trivial minority of patients closer to the competing set in that modality.
This evidence does not itself determine whether the set should be accepted, dropped, split, or merged.
